statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14673 (PostgreSQL amcheck does not clear untrusted search path): a grantee of EXECUTE on an amcheck function can set a hostile search path and run arbitrary functions as the owner of an expression index that depends on it. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14673/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_16_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/2cc14731825ec94017a3717e510f1f6780160c8a (Security: CVE-2026-14673, in tag REL_16_15 and not in REL_16_14), which makes bt_index_check_internal in contrib/amcheck/verify_nbtree.c set search_path to "pg_catalog, pg_temp" while it runs as the index owner. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14673 under 16.15-r0 in its secfixes. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on that branch and the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the current 16.16-r0 build uses the APKBUILD at that commit, and none of its patches changes verify_nbtree.c. We read every published postgresql16 and postgresql16-contrib package for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0) on x86_64 and aarch64: /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in each reports the matching PostgreSQL release, and /usr/lib/postgresql16/amcheck.so in postgresql16-contrib contains the "pg_catalog, pg_temp" setting from the fix in 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0, while 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 lack it. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL states that major version 17 is not affected by CVE-2026-14673 (amcheck does not clear an untrusted search path before running index expressions): https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14673/ lists only versions 18, 16, 15 and 14 as affected and says PostgreSQL 17 is unaffected. The fix commit on the 17 branch, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/e41c72aff0399dd46f3c4f2f7ee242e99ecf0e32, explains why: v17 was already safe, because commit 2af07e2f749a9208ca1ed84fa1d8fe0e75833288 ("Fix search_path to a safe value during maintenance operations", released in PostgreSQL 17.0) already makes amcheck run with a safe search_path, so on the 17 branch the change adds only a regression test and a comment. Every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) is PostgreSQL 17, as its postgres server binary reports on both x86_64 and aarch64, so none of them contains the vulnerable code path. In the upstream source of each 17.x release these builds use, REL_17_7 through REL_17_12, bt_index_check_internal() in contrib/amcheck/verify_nbtree.c sets the safe search_path through RestrictSearchPath() before index expressions run, and none of those releases contains commit d70b17636ddf1ea2c71d1c7bc477372b36ccb66b, the PostgreSQL 18 change that dropped that call. Alpine lists this CVE under its postgresql17 17.11-r0 secfixes and the 17.11 release notes mention it, but on the 17 branch the 17.11 change for it is only that test and comment, so no 17.x build needed a code fix.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14673 (PostgreSQL amcheck does not clear untrusted search path): a grantee of EXECUTE on an amcheck function can run arbitrary functions as the owner of an expression index that depends on the search path. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14673/ lists 18.6 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/0a61fcde03257739d59d9b96e4c77f6c65e070e3 (Security: CVE-2026-14673, in tag REL_18_6 and not in REL_18_4), which adds a RestrictSearchPath() call to amcheck_lock_relation_and_check() in contrib/amcheck/verify_common.c; its message explains that a PostgreSQL 18 change had removed the protection PostgreSQL 17 had. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, say so), so although Alpine's security database lists this CVE for postgresql18 under 18.5-r0, this owner has no 18.5-r0 build and its first build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the 3.23-stable branch of aports (current revision https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD) and the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version; none of the patches that APKBUILD applies, at any revision used for these builds, changes the files this fix changes. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64. We read every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index, and in each the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. amcheck.so ships in the postgresql18-contrib package of every one of those builds on both architectures. In the dynamic symbol table of amcheck.so, the 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 builds import RestrictSearchPath and the earlier builds do not, on both architectures; none of amcheck's source files at the REL_18_4 tag calls it. As a control, every build's amcheck.so imports NewGUCNestLevel, which the same function calls. 18.6-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from PostgreSQL releases before the fix and are affected.
